record.original_question: Do there exist smooth vector fields on R^3 that satisfy the Markus-Yamabe hypothesis that all eigenvalues of DF(x) have negative real part at every point, but nevertheless possess periodic orbits?

evidence.quote: Problem 19. Are there smooth vector fields in R^3 under the hypotheses of the Markus-Yamabe conjecture and having periodic orbits?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Recall the Markus–Yamabe hypothesis on a smooth vector field $F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n$: $F$ has a (unique) equilibrium and, for every $x\in\mathbb{R}^n$, all eigenvalues of the Jacobian matrix $DF(x)$ have negative real part. The classical Markus–Yamabe conjecture asserts that under this hypothesis the equilibrium is a global attractor; this is true in dimension $n=2$ but is known to fail for $n\geq 3$.

Question: Does there exist a smooth vector field $F:\mathbb{R}^3\to\mathbb{R}^3$ satisfying the Markus–Yamabe hypothesis (i.e., all eigenvalues of $DF(x)$ have strictly negative real part for every $x\in\mathbb{R}^3$) whose associated dynamical system $\dot x = F(x)$ admits at least one periodic orbit?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is listed as an open problem in a 2020 collection of open problems in low-dimensional dynamical systems. Known counterexamples to the Markus–Yamabe conjecture in $\mathbb{R}^3$ (e.g., polynomial families) provide trajectories escaping to infinity but, to current knowledge, no smooth example with a genuine periodic orbit under the full Markus–Yamabe spectral hypothesis has been exhibited. No subsequent resolution was found in the search.

status_evidence.title: Some open problems in low dimensional dynamical systems
status_evidence.snippet: Problem 19. Are there smooth vector fields in R^3 under the hypotheses of the Markus-Yamabe conjecture and having periodic orbits?

status_evidence.title: The Discrete and Continuous Markus-Yamabe Stability Conjectures
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing counterexamples to the Markus–Yamabe conjecture in dimension n>=3 and related weak versions.
status_evidence.claim: Counterexamples exist in R^3 but the periodic-orbit version remains a separate question.
